page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon processors clocked at 2.2 GHz, the instance provides hardware virtualization support, AVX instruction set extensions, AES cryptographic acceleration, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It does not include attached local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark results place the multi-threaded capabilities of this instance within the mid-tier spectrum. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 5488.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12431.07, supported by stress-ng multi-core throughput of 21496.93. Memory throughput measures 71.67 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 35.27 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect conservative execution speeds, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 858.0 and lower throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (18.89 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (6.36 GB/sec).

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-16 delivers steady multi-threaded capacity for environments that do not require high memory footprints. Workload throughput tests demonstrate solid operational capacity, handling 15.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.91 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. This makes the machine well configured for parallel compilation tasks, batch data processing, distributed build agents, and microservices hosting where CPU core density takes precedence over large working memory sets.

Designed with a lean 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation, it excludes local storage drives and hardware GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded execution, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 12431.07, 15.91 million Redis SET operations per second, and a Clang compilation score of 9282.0. However, single-threaded processing reflects constrained baseline performance across compression and Geekbench benchmarks. This configuration provides a resource-dense CPU profile suitable for parallelized batch processing, continuous integration build jobs, web traffic routing, and distributed compute workloads where memory demands are predictable and modest.
